The successor immediately consumes that state plus listed public obligations; it has no anchor_policy edge, owns the rebased state as its sole executable ancestry, and emits the sole outward policy.

Treat the immediately preceding executable state as the sole policy ancestry. qualitative_hypothesis.causal_change: Introduce an executable-genesis lineage rebase: the first call materializes a complete policy state as a new root, and the second receives that executable root plus public obligations but no anchor-policy visibility or edit provenance.
qualitative_hypothesis.expected_effect: The independent root should allow scan-resistance and phase-shift adaptation behavior to be formed coherently outside the anchor genealogy while preserving a directly executable lineage.
qualitative_hypothesis.falsifier: all-valid matched majority and strict-median contract, with no score
qualitative_hypothesis.observed_bottleneck: The champion assumes every useful behavior must remain reachable as reversible edits of the anchor, so terminal compression can remove edits but cannot escape the anchor's coupled behavioral commitments.

structural_mutation.after: A founder materializes one complete executable state as a new lineage root, then an anchor-blind successor takes sole constructive custody of that state and emits the final policy.
structural_mutation.before: One anchor-rooted producer retains reversible edit provenance and simplifies the resulting stack through terminal causal compression.
structural_mutation.why_structural: The rebase changes lineage origin, edge visibility, constructive authority, and state-transition semantics rather than splitting or renaming terminal roles.
